title: Ashneel Kumar v. State of U.P. and Another
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Shashi Kant Gupta and Piyush Agrawal, JJ.
disposition: Writ disposed of. Petitioner directed to appear before the Executive Engineer with objections; speaking final order within four weeks; coercive action stayed for seven weeks; liberty to appeal under section 127.
headnote: Without examining alleged want of hearing or breach of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, the Court directed the consumer to appear before the Executive Engineer with objections and evidence, required a speaking and reasoned final order within four weeks, stayed coercive recovery for seven weeks or until disposal of the objection, and left the consumer, if aggrieved by that final order, to appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003. Default in appearance revives the recovery citation.
facts: The petitioner, Ashneel Kumar, challenged a recovery notice dated 19 November 2019 issued by the Executive Engineer (respondent no. 2), seeking certiorari to quash the notice, mandamus to restore his electricity connection, and an interim restraint on coercive recovery. He alleged that the respondents were taking coercive action without an opportunity of hearing and without following the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. The electricity department was represented. The High Court did not examine those allegations on merits.

holding_units.holding: On a writ to quash a recovery notice and restore supply, the Court, taking a lenient view and without deciding alleged non-compliance with the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, directed the consumer to appear before the Executive Engineer with objections and evidence; the Executive Engineer shall pass a speaking and reasoned final order within four weeks; no coercive action for seven weeks or until disposal of the objection, whichever is earlier; if aggrieved by the final order, the consumer may appeal under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003; default in appearance revives the recovery citation. Writ disposed of.

principle_tags.application: After directing the Executive Engineer to pass a speaking final order on the consumer's objection to the recovery notice, the Court left it open to the consumer, if aggrieved, to appeal under section 127 rather than deciding the recovery or restoration on writ merits.

Liberty was expressly reserved to file an appeal before the concerned authority under section 127 of the Electricity Act, 2003 in accordance with law if the consumer is aggrieved by the Executive Engineer's final order.

not_decided.point: Whether the recovery notice dated 19 November 2019 was issued without hearing or in breach of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005
Quashing of the recovery notice and restoration of the electricity connection
not_decided.note: Certiorari and mandamus were prayed; the Court neither granted nor refused those reliefs on merits.
